Trenton Municipal Court

Address: 225 N Clinton Ave, Trenton, NJ 08609, United States

Phone: 609-989-3000

Trenton Municipal Court is a justice center city for all the people in Trenton city. The court is situated in Trenton, United States, at 225 N Clinton Ave. It is a part of the largest judiciary in New Jersey. Its mission is to serve people fairly as an independent branch of government and preserve the rule of law. It protects rights and liberties according to the direction of the United States guaranteed by the constitution. It conducts 24 court sessions per week. The court holds special night court sessions on Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday at 6:30 pm.

Trenton Municipal Court is one of the busiest courts in New Jersey, handling a wide range of cases that include traffic violations, criminal offenses, and municipal ordinance violations. Established in 1918, the court has been providing justice to the residents of Trenton for over a century.

Function of Trenton Municipal Court

The primary function of Trenton Municipal Court is to adjudicate cases that are brought before it. The court handles both criminal and civil cases, with criminal cases ranging from minor traffic offenses to serious criminal offenses. Civil cases that are heard in the court include landlord-tenant disputes, small claims, and code violations.

Importance of Trenton Municipal Court

Trenton Municipal Court is important for several reasons. Firstly, it is responsible for maintaining law and order in Trenton. By ensuring that those who violate the law are held accountable, the court contributes to a safer and more peaceful community. Secondly, the court provides access to justice for all members of the community, regardless of their social or economic status. Finally, the court helps to ensure that the rights of individuals are protected and that justice is served.

Processes of Trenton Municipal Court

The processes of Trenton Municipal Court vary depending on the type of case being heard. However, there are certain general procedures that are followed in most cases. These include:

Filing a Complaint

In order to initiate a case in Trenton Municipal Court, a complaint must be filed. The complaint can be filed by either the police or a private citizen.

Arraignment

The arraignment is the first court appearance for a defendant. During the arraignment, the defendant is informed of the charges against them and advised of their rights.

Plea Bargaining

In many cases, the defendant and the prosecutor will engage in plea bargaining in an attempt to resolve the case without going to trial.

Trial

If the case cannot be resolved through plea bargaining, a trial will be held. During the trial, evidence is presented and witnesses are called to testify.

Sentencing

If the defendant is found guilty, they will be sentenced. Sentences can include fines, probation, community service, or imprisonment.

Court Session

Trenton Municipal Court Session deals with 12 different kinds of matters:

  • Arraignment matters
  • Complaints from citizen matters
  • Trial of citizen matters
  • Violation of City Ordinance
  • Criminal matters
  • DWI matters
  • Housing matters
  • Motions matters
  • Parking matters
  • Special Sessions
  • Traffic matters
  • Truancy matters

Virtual Court:

Trenton Municipal court virtual court is an online hearing facility given by the court due to coronavirus. The hearing is done using Microsoft Teams or telephones. Any person who wants to schedule an online hearing for their case must contact the customer service court, which will give you all the information and schedule.

How To Fine Payment:

Trenton Municipal Court pay fine is done in the following ways:

In-Person

A Person can pay a fine by visiting the court during business hours.

Online

A Person can pay a fine using the online system. The courthouse accepts all online methods.

Mail

A Person can pay a fine by sending a check to the court's mailing address. The court's mailing address is 225 N Clinton Ave, Trenton, NJ 08609, United States.

Form Center:

Trenton Municipal Court Form Center contains all the form information the court provides. The documents can help and guide a person in any case or service. It contains:

  • Appeal Court Decision Form
  • Confidential Complaint Information Form
  • Court Record Request Form
  • Court Transcript Request Form
  • Final Questionnaires Form
  • Request for Waiver Appearance Form

Granting of Adjournments:

Trenton Municipal Court granting of adjournments is a policy of conflicts that permits the municipal court administrative and judge to give adjournment specific consent to an adjournment. It will be granted for the request to be honored by the court. In state cases, When the defendant is not constituted by the council and the state is formed by the private or public prosecutor, the administrator will notify all counsel and parties for the denial or granting of adjournment.

A plea by Affidavit

Trenton Municipal Court Plea Affidavit is a court permit for a defendant to present a defense statement in mitigation by mail if the court considers that a defendant feels difficulty appearing in court. That plea by mail is allowed in all traffic cases except for personal injury in an accident or operation of the vehicle using narcotics or drugs.

A plea by Mail

If you want to make a plea by mail, then you must:

  • Ask the court staff to obtain approval to forward the defense by mail.
  • Fill out the form for the plea by mail according to the instruction.
  • The prosecution will give its testimony routinely, and the content of the affidavit will be read in the open court by the judge.
  • Ruling in the case will be provided by the judge, and a message of disposition will be sent by the Clerk using mail.
  • You will be directed to comply if a sentence is imposed within ten days.

FAQ

Which type of violation required a personal appearance in court?

A violation that requires a personal appearance in court is:

  • · Drive while using alcohol/drugs
  • · Drive while suspended
  • · Offenses like drugs or Paraphernalia
  • · Leave from the scene of the accident
  • · Avoiding or fleeing a police officer
  • · Pass by a standing school bus
  • · In 12 months, you do a third moving violation

What are the form filling fees?

Trenton Municipal Court Form Filings fees depend upon the form a person is filing. For example, $100 is the filing fee for the transcript for appeal in court.

What will the public defender do?

Trenton Municipal Court Public Defender will tell or determine the court that you cannot afford an attorney when you are charged with an indictable offense.

When will you present your witness on your behalf?

You will present your witness on your behalf after the prosecution is finished. It is not compulsory to testify yourself; it’s your wish to testify or not.

How many days do I appeal if I feel an error in my case result?

If you feel the case result has an error, you should appeal within twenty days. The Superior Court law division will hear the appeal.

How do I dispute parking tickets?

Notify the court administrator about your intention at least seven days before your court date; otherwise, you must make two court appearances. Visit the court during business hours or contact them by telephone.

What is the price of my ticket?

The price of tickets will be found on the back of the tickets you received. The violation Bureau also contains all the ticket prices you may contact them.

Where do I get a copy of a police report?

You can get a copy of the police report at the Trenton police department, bubble front desk, situated at 225 N Clinton Avenue, Trenton, NJ 08609.

Who do I call to check my court date?

Call the court staff; they will tell you your court date.

Phone: 609-989-3700.

What to do if I need an interpreter?

Tell the person who calls your name that you need an interpreter when you first visit the court. Specify the language in which you want an interpreter.
